Subject: POC Kickstart - availability tango & acceptance gates

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the time on the call yesterday. We’re excited to get the POC moving. To make the kickoff efficient for your cross-functional team, can we align on an initial meeting that covers success criteria, timeline, and owners? Below are two proposed windows (PT):

- Option A: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 — 09:00–11:00 (2h)
- Option B: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 — 14:00–16:00 (2h)

Proposed kickoff agenda (45–90m core + buffer):
- Introductions & roles (10m)
- POC scope & success criteria (20m)
- Network/security checklist & procurement timeline (20m)
- Demo plan & test data needs (20m)
- Next steps / owners / timeline (10m)

Success criteria (high level):
- End-to-end inference on a representative dataset with <200ms median token latency for the critical route.
- Integration test: host app can call Redwood API and verify token-level billing and tracing headers.
- Security: agreed data flow and documentation for SOC2/compliance reviewers.

Prep we’ll attach: POC_Scope_v1.pdf and NetworkRequirements.xlsx. Can you confirm who from TerraLab needs to attend (engineering, procurement, security)? If neither of these windows works, please suggest two alternatives and we’ll triage with the SE and procurement owners.

Thanks — Priya

SE prep checklist (who does what before Jan 6):
- Redwood (Mina) — validate sample payloads, provide a short demo script, and confirm expected median token latency on our test model.
- TerraLab (Engineering lead) — provide representative dataset sample (anonymized) and a service account for API integration testing.
- Procurement (Leah) — confirm DocuSign workflow for the term sheet and timeline for signatures.

Success criteria (technical detail):
- End-to-end inference executed with TerraLab sample, median per-token latency < 200ms on the tested route (90%+ of requests).
- API call surface validated: authentication, tracing headers, error-handling behavior for 5xx scenarios.
- Cost telemetry visible on Redbox console and match expected token counts within 10%.
